claim: Parameter-based knowledge editing cannot reliably update factual knowledge in a large language model without damaging its core capabilities. The near-perfect editing results reported in prior work do not survive realistic evaluation, and the limitation is geometric rather than incidental: localized weight edits are disproportionately amplified along low-variance directions of the model's representation space and propagate globally, so damage compounds as edits accumulate. A parameter-free approach that leaves the weights untouched is therefore a serious alternative to parameter editing rather than a fallback.
experiments_evaluated: To address subclaims 1, 2, 5, and 6—whether parameter editing is reliable under realistic evaluation, whether prior near-perfect results survive, whether edits propagate globally, and whether damage compounds—run a preregistered sequential no-rollback benchmark using public COUNTERFACT and ZSRE data from Hugging Face. Apply ROME, MEMIT, MEND, unconstrained fine-tuning, and constrained fine-tuning to GPT-2 XL and GPT-J, retaining 1, 10, 100, and 1000 edits cumulatively; tune each method only on a disjoint validation split. At every checkpoint measure reliability on canonical edit prompts, generalization on paraphrases, COUNTERFACT ES/PS/NS, portability on subject-replacement, reversed, and one-hop probes, and locality on both relation-matched and random out-of-scope prompts. Measure global damage with output-distribution KL divergence, perplexity on WikiText-103, and accuracy on public HellaSwag, LAMBADA, Natural Questions, and an appropriate public MMLU release. Filter facts the base model cannot recall, validate generated prompts, report bootstrap confidence intervals, and compare cumulative editing with isolated rollback evaluation. Broadly distributed prediction changes or monotonic losses in locality and general capabilities as edit count rises—especially while canonical reliability remains high—would support the claim and explain why earlier headline scores were misleading. Stable reliability, paraphrase/portability performance, locality, perplexity, and downstream accuracy through large edit counts would refute or sharply qualify it; failure confined to one editor, dataset, layer, or backbone would indicate an incidental implementation issue rather than a general limitation. This experiment could be unnecessary if prior work released complete no-rollback trajectories, checkpoints, prompts, and downstream evaluations for the same cross-method and cross-backbone design, allowing independent reanalysis.

To address subclaims 3 and 4—whether the limitation is geometric and whether localized edits are amplified along low-variance representation directions—analyze the checkpoints and edits from the first experiment. For each edited layer and subject-token location, estimate the pre-edit activation covariance on a large public corpus such as WikiText-103, using held-out samples and shrinkage or randomized low-rank eigendecomposition. Decompose both the editor's weight update and its induced activation change into covariance-eigenvector bins, then calculate variance-normalized gain: the change in downstream hidden states, logits, and output KL per unit update norm for high-, middle-, and low-variance bins. Test global propagation on unrelated COUNTERFACT/ZSRE prompts and WikiText text by tracing each component through all later layers. Establish causality rather than correlation by applying norm-matched synthetic low-rank perturbations aligned with low-variance versus high-variance eigendirections, selecting magnitudes small enough to match the original edit's efficacy, and compare their downstream amplification and capability damage. Sweep layers, token positions, corruption magnitudes, and tracing aggregation rules; repeat localization with representation zeroing; and fit mixed-effects regressions predicting locality or downstream damage from inverse representation variance while controlling for layer, update norm, editor, relation, model, and edit count. Consistently larger gain and wider output changes for low-variance-aligned components, plus superior prediction of cumulative damage after controls, would support a geometric mechanism. Equal amplification across variance bins, disappearance under norm/layer controls, or dependence on one tracing procedure would reject or weaken that mechanism even if editing still fails empirically. This experiment could be replaced by released per-edit weight deltas, representative activation statistics, and downstream Jacobian or propagation measurements sufficient to reproduce the eigenspace analysis.

To address subclaims 7 and 8—whether a parameter-free approach leaves base weights untouched and is a serious alternative—compare IKE-style in-context editing and retrieval-backed external memory with ROME, MEMIT, MEND, and constrained fine-tuning on the same public COUNTERFACT, ZSRE, and, if available on Hugging Face, MQuAKE splits and the same GPT-2 XL/GPT-J backbones. Before and after every parameter-free edit, verify bitwise hashes of all base-model tensors, optimizer state, and model configuration; separately report any external index, stored demonstrations, or added module parameters so that 'weights untouched' is not confused with zero storage. Match methods by edit set and evaluate canonical reliability, paraphrase generalization, relation/subject portability, multi-hop propagation, out-of-scope locality, WikiText-103 perplexity, HellaSwag/LAMBADA/Natural Questions performance, latency, context-token cost, memory, and persistence across sessions. Run 1–1000 cumulative edits, include retrieval-disabled and irrelevant-memory controls, and evaluate both with and without the edited fact literally present in the final prompt to detect copying. A parameter-free method that preserves exact base-weight hashes and is Pareto-competitive in reliability, robust generalization, locality, accumulated damage, and practical resource cost would establish it as a serious alternative; success only through verbatim prompt insertion, severe context or latency costs, retrieval leakage, or poor portability would make it a limited fallback. If weight editors remain equally stable and substantially more accurate or efficient, the comparative claim would be refuted. This experiment could be unnecessary if existing studies provide auditable tensor hashes, external-storage accounting, matched sequential evaluations, and full quality-versus-resource Pareto results.
reference_experiments: Fix the measurement floor and the inference protocol before editing anything. Score the unedited model on the editing benchmark to establish the pre-edit baseline, and re-run single-edit evaluation of existing methods under plain autoregressive decoding rather than the teacher-forced protocol prior work used, since teacher forcing supplies the ground-truth answer tokens at inference and inflates every number. If methods keep their near-perfect single-edit scores under honest decoding there is no discrepancy to explain. The authors report a pre-edit baseline of Reliability 3.00, Generalization 3.00, Locality 15.50, Portability 4.36 on ZsRE, and a best parameter-based single-edit average of 25.99.

Validate the scoring instrument before quoting any number from it. Judge semantic consistency of generated answers with a strong LLM across reliability, generalization, locality and portability, then cross-check that ranking with a deterministic token-level measure (match ratio and exact match) that does not depend on a model's opinion. If the two disagree, every result is an artifact of the judge rather than a property of the editing methods. The authors find the token-level check reproduces the semantic ranking, with the pre-edit model at 100% by definition and GRACE holding 100% under both single and sequential editing.

Test the asserted mechanism directly. Take the SVD of the original hidden-representation matrix, compute the directional relative change rate R_k = sqrt(n)|u_k^T delta_h| / sigma_k for each principal direction after an edit, and check where amplification concentrates and how it behaves as edits accumulate. The claim's causal story requires R_k > 1 predominantly in low-singular-value directions with the fraction rising monotonically with edit count, across methods and architectures.

Run the main benchmark. Compare eleven editing methods spanning locate-then-edit (ROME, MEMIT, PMET, RECT, AlphaEdit, FT-L), meta-learning (MEND), additional-parameter (AdaLoRA, WISE) and external-memory (GRACE, SCR) families, under sequential editing at 1, 10, 100 and full-dataset edit counts, on ZsRE and WikiData-counterfact, across Llama-2-7B-Chat, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, reporting all four dimensions. The claim holds if every parameter-modifying method degrades toward zero as edits accumulate and the parameter-free retrieval baseline outscores all of them; the authors report ROME, RECT, FT-L, MEND and AdaLoRA at 0.00-0.25 average under sequential editing on DeepSeek-R1-Distill, against SCR at 56.59 single and 60.19 sequential.

Measure damage to capabilities the edits never targeted. Take the models edited in the main benchmark and evaluate them on mathematical reasoning (AIME 2024, AIME 2025, AMC, OlympiadBench, MATH-500) and broad benchmarks (GPQA-Diamond, ARC-c, MMLU-Pro), reporting accuracy after 10 and after 100 sequential edits. Without this the study would only show editing is ineffective, not that it is damaging. The authors report ROME and RECT losing 2.74 and 8.37 average accuracy at 10 edits and falling to near zero at 100, with MEND at 0.00 after both.

Rule out that the result is an artifact of scale, knowledge type, fact difficulty or one method's configuration. Repeat the sweep on larger models (Llama-2-13B, Qwen3-14B), on event-level knowledge (ELKEN, with events converted to triples for the parameter-based arms), split by high- and low-confidence fact sets, and probe the hyperparameter and architecture sensitivity of AlphaEdit — the one method that does not collapse — including its failure to run on Llama-2 and Mistral. If the collapse disappears at 13-14B or only occurs on triple-shaped facts, the claim is bounded rather than general.
